profile.headline: Software Engineer II @ HAVIK | VR Training
profile.summary:
I'm a dedicated XR Software Engineer with 4 years of professional experience, passionate about the intersection of technology and immersive experiences. A graduate from Atlas School '22 and the University of Tulsa '17, I bring a unique blend of technical skills and creative problem-solving to the world of augmented and virtual reality.

Professional Journey
Currently, I specialize in developing augmented and virtual reality applications for platforms like Oculus, iOS, Android, and WebXR. I find the immersive nature of XR technologies incredibly compelling, as they offer unparalleled retention and emotional engagement compared to traditional media.

A few cool bits about me, I've been to 15 National Parks, 48 States, and I used to know the capital of every country on Earth (still remember quite a bit though). I used to work in the art world and I found out that explaining complex overviews of code is like explaining a work of art.

positions.title: Software Engineer II
positions.description: HAVIK provides fully portable, self-contained virtual reality (VR) training solutions for military training. Developed in close collaboration with experienced operators, HAVIK provides trainees with high fidelity, mobile simulations for immersive training at any time or in any location. The HAVIK ecosystem allows trainees to work independently, with an instructor, or with a diverse group across the globe!

positions.title: Freelance Software Engineer - iOS, Android, Augmented Reality
positions.description:
I work with organizations and people to explore creative options that augmented reality can solve, how this works.
- I can teach C-Suite people what AR is and how memory retention is higher than video format.
- I collaborate concept, develop, and project management to a product timeline.
- Evaluate the KPIs

positions.title: Software Engineering Student - Augmented and Virtual Reality
positions.description:
Atlas School is a peer-learning vocational coding school. You and your cohort work together to complete projects for 18-months. I added this to explain the career change I went through, as it took 70 - 80 hours a week of studying to be proficient.

I learned a survey of foundational computer science, time management, and how to develop software for augmented and virtual reality experiences.

positions.title: Communication Manager
positions.description: I helped modernize communications, managed the website, social media, and communication timelines for 200+ events.

positions.title: Communication Intern
positions.description: I managed and executed public relations strategies for a non-profit art gallery. I worked with the local media to promote exhibitions, the Day of the Dead Arts Festival, and the Champagne and Chocolate Gala.

positions.title: Partner Trainer
positions.description: I developed and challenged partners to fit their potential.

educations.degreeName: Computer Science; Augmented and Virtual Reality
educations.fieldOfStudy: Computer Science; Augmented and Virtual Reality

honors.title: Hackathon Finalist - Second Place
honors.description: My team and I won second place in Tulsa's first community hackathon hosted by CLLCTVE. Our idea was to reimagine the existing app Spatial, but as a matching space for creators and brands in VR.

volunteerExperiences.description: I help facilitate networking events and foster community for the local tech scene in Tulsa.

projects.title: ParkPort
projects.description: A smartphone application that utilizes geolocation to guide the user to explore Tulsa's parks and collect augmented reality stamps

projects.title: VR Escape Room
projects.description:
I learned how to script interactable objects in a VR environment!
How to test in VR. How to optimize for VR. How to create a 3d world that doesn't break immersion.
It was a lot of fun and I learned how Unity takes in inputs from the XR plugin manager from all the different types of VR headsets.
